reportedBy: user, TUI mode: (1) the full-screen panel's horizontal scrollbar cannot be dragged with the mouse; (2) the frame sometimes tears/deforms, and once deformed the scrollbar is unusable (screenshot /home/haroldzhao/MyProj/DshProj/tempfile/sidebarerror.png, sha256 d1457d57…)

diagnosis.railInteraction: No scene carried any drag handler; onDragStart/onDragMove/onDragEnd existed only in panel-core.ts (the sidebar pages). The horizontal rails were bare Text elements (scenes.ts 'hrail', subagent-scene.ts 'hrail'), so no element could carry a pointer handler at all.
diagnosis.tearing: Scenes built body rows and rails at the RAW terminal columns while surfaceFrame spends 2 border + 2 paddingX cells, and surfaceText never forwarded maxCells to textRow. The host WRAPS an over-wide Text, so each overflow added a visual row the vertical window (which counts ELEMENTS, not visual rows) never subtracted: the frame grew past the terminal and the rail's shade cells spilled into neighbouring rows. The merged scene additionally built its DAG slice, rail and legend 4 cells over the interior.
diagnosis.rejectedAndReverted: An intermediate implementation gated the DAG-vs-rail choice on 'the natural drawing fits the interior', which made the team scene's horizontal band unreachable by construction (layoutRail is exactly graphWidth wide) — i.e. it DELETED the scrollbar the user asked to drag. Reverted to the shipped rule (boxes whenever two node columns fit, the rest reached by horizontal pan) and the contract was amended (W4-AMENDED).

bounds: No live TTY and no real-mouse capture: the proof is the rendered element tree plus the package suite, exactly as the sidebar's drag arms are proved.
The horizontal rail carries no onClick (three drag phases only), because that is what the sidebar's shared viewportRail offers; adding click-to-position there would also change the sidebar page.

The subagents scene deliberately has NO vertical rail: it has no viewport-height window to describe, so a vertical bar there would report a band that does not exist. Its uncapped vertical tail therefore stays PARKED (§11.12).

The sidebar plane's width accounting was NOT defective (panelFrame has no paddingX; the pages draw at cols-3 and already ship a row-fit arm), so this wave does not claim to have fixed any sidebar tearing; a sidebar-side report would need its own capture.
The corner shade residue of the reported capture may additionally involve host repaint across a width change; no fixed-size PTY capture was made, so that part stays a declared bound.
The BOARD scene's scroll plumbing moved onto `usePanelViewport` (behaviour-preserving, but listed so the change is not silent).

The reported capture's title format matches no surface in this tree and it shows no frame border, so it cannot be tied to a build; the wrap mechanism it is consistent with is proved here, not the exact frame.
